units.translation: Donaldson (New Cratylus p. 269) discussed this passage, interpreting it as “from excessive credulity the boundaries of a woman's mind are easily encroached upon". For similar examples of figurative usage see Thes. vol. 3 p. 1709.
The female boundary, too persuasive, is encroached upon swiftly.
victory song
a song by which victory is celebrated
shouting victory songs
to distribute
I distribute
In tmesis
A stranger, a settler from Scythia, distributes the lots of steel.
How faction distributes the lots of mortals.
And he directs everything to its end.
to call to witness
I call to witness
Sophocles in the Assembly of the Achaeans (fr. 158) and Aeschylus in the Cretan Women (fr. 116).
I call to witness these things, as one about to die.
to call to witness: to testify, to go.
Sophocles in the Assembly of the Achaeans
and Aeschylus in the Cretan Women
kitchen table
kitchen table
Instead of the ancestral altar, a kitchen table awaits.
to brandish
I brandish
Ares brandishing his weapons.
all
all
where it must be noted that the last syllable is lengthened. The scholiast took it as an adverb (wholly), those who dwell throughout the mainland.
where the scholiast explains it as equal upon all.
and those who occupy the mainland-born race entirely
and your yoke of the balance is wholly
those who dwell throughout the mainland
equal upon all
to be persuaded, to be convinced
I am persuaded, I am convinced
For I am persuaded by these testimonies.
to chastise, to reproach
I chastise, I reproach
Do not reproach me for my stubbornness and harshness of temper.
to blow upon, to inspire
I blow upon, I inspire
And raging Ares, tamer of peoples, breathes upon.
inspiration
inspiration
Our race, from the touch and inspiration of Zeus of the gadfly-driven cow, has been fulfilled in prayer.
and the offspring of the flower-grazing ancestral cow, from the inspiration of Zeus, the touch.
with unharmed strength and divine inspirations it ceases.
to fly over
I fly over. In tmesis.
For some Stygian mist has flown over.
Such darkness of pollution has flown over the man.
to cause to fall to someone
I cause something to fall to someone
Intransitively, I fall to, I happen
Justice causes the future to fall to those who have suffered, for them to learn.
You would not justly bring any wrath upon this city.
the wedding song, which then fell to the bridegrooms to sing.
But if necessity of this fortune falls upon us.
to flow in
I flow in
For the time flowing in will be more honored.
to tear
I tear
And she tore her robe over the misfortune of evil.
to throw upon, to impose
I throw upon, I impose
For a god, wishing to unite with this mortal woman, threw upon her these wanderings.
influx
influx
And dark Ares is forced by kindred streams of blood.
With evil influxes and with mud defiling bright water, you will never find a drink.
O Caicus and Mysian streams.
to shout in response
I shout in response, as Hesychius explains ἐπερρόθησαν by ἐπήχησαν, ἐπεβόησαν.
And with a din it shouts in response to my beaten and utterly wretched head.
And this all-common faction shouts in response.
they shouted in response
they sounded, they shouted
bringing aid, helping
bringing aid, helping
There is hope that the nocturnal end of all-lamentable woes will come as a helper.
to command with a hoarse voice
I command with a hoarse voice
